title: New at the Table
subtitle: Six sessions for the first weeks of a brand new faith, run around a table by the person who pointed the way
summary: When someone comes to faith, the worst thing we can do is hand them a building and a schedule and walk away. The first weeks decide a great deal. This study is for the believer who led a friend to Jesus, or is walking beside a brand new one, and wants to ground them in the things that hold: who they now are, what the cross actually did, the Spirit who lives in them, how to talk to the Father, how to live on the Word, and how, sooner than they think, they will be the one pointing the way for someone else. It is built for a kitchen table, not a classroom. Keep it slow, keep it warm, and keep it moving outward.
setting: A home, a kitchen table, a coffee shop booth. Two people, or a few. Bibles open, phones down, no stage and no script to perform.
forWho: A brand new believer and the friend walking with them. Also useful for anyone who never had a foundation laid and quietly knows it.
rhythm: Open with a question. Read a short passage out loud. Notice what it says. Talk it over honestly. Practice one thing before you meet again. Send each other out with a single sentence. Then ask who each of you could bring next.
leaderNote: You are not running a class. You are doing for someone what you wish someone had done for you. A few things. Go first with your own honesty, every time, or the table will stay shallow. Do not lecture. The new believer learns more from watching you love Jesus than from anything you explain. Do not pretend you have it figured out. When they ask a question you cannot answer, say so, and go find the answer together. Keep the Bible open and let it do the work rather than your opinions. Above all, from the first session, hold the end in view: this person is not a project to finish but a disciple who will soon make another. Plant that from day one, and you will raise a multiplier instead of a consumer.

sessions.title: You Are In
sessions.bigIdea: The first word of the new life is not try harder. It is welcome home. You did not earn your way in, and you cannot earn your way back out.
sessions.open: Tell each other about a time you were welcomed somewhere you were not sure you belonged. What did it feel like when you realized you were actually wanted there?
sessions.read: Read John 1:12-13 out loud, slowly. To all who received him, who believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of God. Then read Romans 8:15-16. You did not receive a spirit of slavery to fall back into fear. You received the Spirit of adoption, and by him we cry out to God as Father.
observe: According to John, what makes a person a child of God, and what does not?
Romans says the new life is the opposite of slavery and fear. What word does it use for what we received instead?
talk: Adoption means a chosen, permanent belonging that does not depend on your performance. What in you still expects God to love you based on how well you do?
If you are already fully in, already a child, what changes about why you would obey God at all?
Where have you been carrying fear that a child of a good Father does not need to carry?
sessions.practice: Each morning this week, before your feet hit the floor, say one true sentence out loud: I am a child of God, and that is settled. Notice what it does to the rest of the day.
sessions.send: You are not auditioning for a place at the table. You are already a son, already a daughter. Live like it.
sessions.passItOn: Who is one person in your life who has never once felt welcomed by God or his people? Write their name down and start praying for them tonight.

sessions.title: What the Cross Did
sessions.bigIdea: The cross is not a sad symbol or a moral example. It is the place where your debt was paid and the exchange was made.
sessions.open: Tell each other about a time someone forgave you a real debt, or took a hit that should have landed on you. How did it change the way you saw them?
sessions.read: Read Isaiah 53:4-6 out loud. He was pierced for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities, and the punishment that brought us peace was on him. Written seven centuries before Jesus. Then read 2 Corinthians 5:21. God made him who knew no sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.
observe: In Isaiah, who carries the wrong, and who goes free?
In 2 Corinthians, name the exchange. What did Jesus take, and what did you receive in its place?
talk: Many people believe Jesus was a good teacher who died unfairly. The Bible says he died on purpose, in your place. Why does the difference matter for your whole life?
If your sin was already fully paid at the cross, what does that do to the guilt you have been dragging around?
The exchange runs both ways. He took your sin, and you received his standing with God. Which half is harder for you to believe, and why?
sessions.practice: This week, name one specific thing you have felt guilty about for a long time. Tell God plainly that you know the cross already covered it, and thank him. Tell your table partner you did it.
sessions.send: There is nothing left on your account that the cross did not already settle. Walk in the clear.
sessions.passItOn: Most people you know misunderstand the cross. Practice saying the exchange in one plain sentence to your table partner, so you are ready when a friend asks.

sessions.title: The Spirit Who Lives in You
sessions.bigIdea: You were not handed a rulebook and left alone to keep it. God himself moved in, and he is the one who grows the new life from the inside.
sessions.open: Tell each other about a habit or change you tried to force by willpower and could not hold. What ran out?
sessions.read: Read John 14:16-17. Jesus promises another Helper to be with you forever, the Spirit of truth, who dwells with you and will be in you. Then read Galatians 5:22-25. The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control.
observe: Where does Jesus say the Helper will be, not just near you but where?
Galatians calls these qualities fruit, not works. What is the difference between fruit that grows and works you grind out?
talk: Fruit grows from a living root over time. It cannot be faked or forced. How does that change the pressure you may feel to instantly become a different person?
The Spirit grows this from the inside, but Galatians still says to keep in step with him. What does cooperating with the Spirit look like on an ordinary day?
Which one piece of that fruit do you most long to see grow in you, and where would your closest people most want to see it?
sessions.practice: Each day this week, before a hard moment, pray six words: Holy Spirit, I cannot. You can. Then watch for him to do what your willpower never could.
sessions.send: You are not alone in this and you were never meant to grind it out. The God who saved you now lives in you to grow you.
sessions.passItOn: Tell your table partner about one place this week you saw the Spirit do something in you that you could not have done yourself.

sessions.title: Talking to the Father
sessions.bigIdea: Prayer is not a performance for an audience or a spell to get things. It is a child talking with a Father who is already glad to listen.
sessions.open: Tell each other what you assumed prayer was before this. Awkward, formal, pointless, only for emergencies? Be honest.
sessions.read: Read Matthew 6:6-13, where Jesus teaches his friends to pray. Notice he tells them to go to a private place and talk to their Father simply, not to pile up fancy words. Then read Philippians 4:6-7. Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer let your requests be made known to God, and the peace of God will guard your heart.
observe: In Matthew, what does Jesus say not to do when you pray, and what does he say to do instead?
Philippians connects prayer to something specific that it guards. What is it?
talk: Jesus calls God Father and tells us to pray plainly. What would change if you stopped performing in prayer and just talked?
The Lord's Prayer moves from God's name and kingdom to daily bread and forgiveness. What does that order teach us about what to ask for first?
Where is the anxiety in your life right now that Philippians is inviting you to hand over instead of carry?
sessions.practice: Pray every day this week, even badly, even for two minutes. Use the Lord's Prayer as a frame if you get stuck. The goal is not eloquence. It is showing your face to your Father daily.
sessions.send: You do not have to get the words right. You have to come. Your Father is already listening.
sessions.passItOn: Pray out loud together before you leave, each of you, even one sentence. Learning to pray with another person is how you will one day teach someone else.

sessions.title: Living on the Word
sessions.bigIdea: The Bible is not a textbook to master. It is bread to live on and a voice to know, the main way your Father speaks and you are formed.
sessions.open: Tell each other about something you read or heard so often that it shaped how you think without you noticing. What forms us when we are not watching?
sessions.read: Read Psalm 1:1-3. The blessed one delights in the law of the Lord and meditates on it day and night, and is like a tree planted by streams of water that yields its fruit in season. Then read 2 Timothy 3:16-17. All Scripture is breathed out by God and useful for teaching, correcting, and training, so that the man of God may be complete.
observe: Psalm 1 compares the person rooted in the Word to a tree by water. What does the tree have that a plant in dry ground does not?
Second Timothy lists what Scripture is useful for. Name the four things, and what they are all aiming at.
talk: A tree by the stream is not straining to produce fruit. It is simply drawing on a steady source. How could daily time in the Word become a stream rather than a chore?
Scripture corrects as well as comforts. Are you willing to let it tell you something you do not want to hear? What makes that hard?
Where do you most need God to speak right now, and where in the Bible might you go to listen?
sessions.practice: Read one chapter of the Gospel of John each day this week. Before you read, ask God to speak. After, write down one sentence he showed you. Bring your six sentences to the next table.
sessions.send: You will not drift into knowing God. You will be planted by the stream on purpose, a little each day, and grow.
sessions.passItOn: Show your table partner exactly how you find a passage and read it. The skill of opening the Bible with someone is a gift you will hand on many times.

sessions.title: Now You Go
sessions.bigIdea: You were never meant to be the end of the line. The table that fed you now sends you to set one of your own. A disciple makes a disciple.
sessions.open: Look back over these six weeks. Tell each other one thing that is different in you now from when you started.
sessions.read: Read Matthew 28:18-20, where Jesus sends his friends to go and make disciples of all nations, teaching them to obey everything he commanded, and promises to be with them always. Then read 2 Timothy 2:2. What you have heard, entrust to faithful people who will be able to teach others also.
observe: In Matthew, the command is not go and make converts but go and make what?
Second Timothy describes a chain of how many generations passing the faith along? Count them.
talk: You are proof that an ordinary believer can help another person follow Jesus. Who in your life is one or two steps behind where you were six weeks ago?
Making a disciple is not having all the answers. It is doing for someone else what was just done for you. What part of that feels possible, and what part scares you?
Second Timothy hands the faith down a chain of four generations. What would it mean for you to not be where the chain stops?
sessions.practice: Pick one person this month and invite them to start this same study with you, with you now in the leader's seat. You are ready enough. You will learn the rest by doing it.
sessions.send: You came to this table hungry, and you were fed. Now go and set a table for someone else. The Lord goes with you, to the very end.
sessions.passItOn: Name the person out loud right now. Set a date to ask them this week. Tell your table partner so they can check in and pray.
